Per-area pollution burden

Source: R/ahlth.R
polbrdarea.Rd

Applies polbrdn to every row of a table with one row per area (forward sortation area, census tract, neighbourhood, ...) and returns the rows sorted by attributable cases, worst first: where in a city or region the pollution burden falls.

Usage

polbrdarea(
  areatab,
  areacol = "fsa",
  expcol = "exposure",
  popcol = "population",
  basratecol = "brate",
  poll = "NO2",
  y = "allcause",
  rare = FALSE,
  hirate = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'polbrdarea'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

areatab

A data frame with one row per area: a label, the exposure in micrograms per cubic metre, the population in persons and the baseline rate per person-year.

areacol, expcol, popcol, basratecol

Column names (single strings) of the label, exposure, population and rate; defaults "fsa", "exposure", "population" and "brate".

poll, y, rare, hirate

Passed to polbrdn for every area.

x

An object of class polbrdarea.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class polbrdarea with one row per area, sorted by attrcases, largest first: the four input columns plus rr, paf, attrcases and basecases.

Details

Each area is treated as wholly exposed at its own concentration (expoprev = 1), with the pollutant's default reference concentration. Every area is checked as polbrdn checks a single population, and the first area that fails stops the call with that area's error. Refusals: a column name that is not a single string or not in the table, an empty table, and a non-numeric exposure, population or rate column. The area labels can be of any type.

See also

expconcidx for how the burden is spread across income.

Examples

# simulated areas
t <- data.frame(fsa = c("A1", "B2"), exposure = c(28, 18),
                population = c(40000, 60000), brate = 0.008)
polbrdarea(t)
#> Pollution burden by area: 2 areas, 18.75 attributable of 800 cases (2.34%)
#>  fsa exposure population brate    rr     paf attrcases basecases
#>   A1       28      40000 0.008 1.036 0.03502    11.205       320
#>   B2       18      60000 0.008 1.016 0.01572     7.544       480
try(polbrdarea(t[, c("fsa", "exposure")]))
#> Error : polbrdarea: areatab missing columns: population, brate.
